page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-4-lssd is a memory-oriented virtual instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor clocked at 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 4 dedicated vCPUs split across 2 physical cores with hyperthreading. It is equipped with 31 GB of system memory, providing 7.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. The CPU features a 504 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and advanced instruction sets including Intel AMX tile and int8 extensions, AVX-512, and hardware AES acceleration. No GPU hardware is included.

Storage capabilities include a bundled 402 GB local NVMe SSD, delivering low-latency disk I/O directly attached to the host. The instance does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 networking addresses, relying on Google Cloud VPC network routing.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded text and compression performance, with single-threaded gzip compression reaching 35.55 GB/sec and Geekbench text processing achieving 2828 points. General PassMark CPU and single-core stress-ng tests indicate average mid-tier capability, while Redis SET operations sustain 7.38 million operations per second. However, overall multi-core scalability and uncached memory bandwidth reflect the lower 4-vCPU profile, registering in lower comparative quartiles during heavy multi-threaded compiles and large-block memory read cycles.

From a resource utilization standpoint, the machine offers high memory density and high-speed local disk capacity without the cost of high core counts. The c4-highmem-4-lssd is suited for memory-intensive caching clusters, Redis deployments, small-to-medium database instances, and localized data transformation pipelines that rely on rapid local storage.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-4-lssd is an x86_64 compute instance designed for memory-intensive and local disk-dependent applications. Driven by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor operating at 2.3 GHz, it features 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 31 GB of system memory, and a 402 GB local NVMe SSD. The processor supports advanced extensions such as AVX-512, Intel AMX, and AES-NI, but does not include GPU resources. Performance testing shows strong single-threaded compression and text processing throughput alongside an average Redis SET rate of 7.38 million operations per second, though multi-core computing and uncached memory bandwidth remain limited by the core count. This resource profile suits memory-bound workloads, Redis caching tiers, lightweight relational databases, and data preprocessing tasks requiring fast ephemeral storage.
